questions.text: What does inverse real-time factor (RTFx) measure for an audio system?

options.A: The delay between the last user word and the first audible response.
options.B: The fraction of generated words matching the reference transcript.
options.C: The mean listener rating of the generated audio’s naturalness.
options.D: The number of audio seconds processed per wall-clock second.

questions.explanation: RTFx is throughput: audio duration divided by processing time. It differs from first-token or first-audio latency.

questions.text: A new ASR model improves overall WER, but users with certain accents report worse recognition. What should the evaluation report add?

options.A: Only the new model’s total parameter count.
options.B: WER by relevant accent slices on a representative held-out set.
options.C: Only the fastest processing time observed.
options.D: A smaller test set containing only the majority accent.

questions.explanation: Aggregate WER can hide subgroup regressions. Slice-level evaluation reveals which users experience worse recognition.

questions.text: The toy ttr_wer function returns sum(per_utterance_WERs) / number_of_utterances. Two utterances have 1 error in 2 reference words and 1 error in 10 reference words. What does it return?

options.B: 0.6, the sum of the two rates.
options.D: 0.2, the mean error count divided by 5.

questions.explanation: The function averages utterance rates: (1/2 + 1/10)/2 = 0.3. It does not aggregate total errors over total reference words, which would give 2/12.
